subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Information Paradox
description: Learn The Information Paradox in one minute.

hook.text: Quantum mechanics says information can never be destroyed. Black holes seem to erase it completely. Who's right?

buildup.text: When matter falls into a black hole, all details about it vanish behind the event horizon—seemingly forever.

discovery.text: If the black hole evaporates via Hawking radiation, the information should come out. But Hawking's math shows it doesn't.

twist.text: Hawking bet against information escaping. In 2004, he conceded—admitting information is likely preserved somehow.

climax.text: Current ideas suggest information may be encoded on the event horizon surface—a concept called the holographic principle.

punchline.text: Does the universe remember everything? Black holes hold the answer.

quiz.question: What is the black hole information paradox?
options: Quantum mechanics says information is preserved, but black holes seem to destroy it
Black holes emit more information than they absorb
We cannot determine the mass of black holes from outside observations

details.summary: If black holes evaporate via Hawking radiation, what happens to the information about everything they swallowed? Quantum mechanics says information cannot be destroyed, but Hawking radiation appears thermal and featureless. This information paradox has driven decades of theoretical debate.
details.whyItMatters: The information paradox forces a confrontation between general relativity and quantum mechanics. Resolving it could reveal the true nature of quantum gravity — making it one of theoretical physics' most important open problems.
takeaways: Quantum mechanics says information cannot be destroyed
Hawking radiation appears to carry no information out
Resolving this paradox could unlock quantum gravity

faq.question: Did Hawking change his mind about information loss?
faq.answer: Yes. Hawking initially argued information was truly lost, but by 2004 he conceded that information is probably preserved and encoded in the radiation through subtle quantum correlations. He famously conceded a bet with John Preskill. The exact mechanism remains debated.

faq.question: What are proposed solutions to the paradox?
faq.answer: Leading proposals include information encoded in Hawking radiation via subtle correlations, holographic principle (information stored on the horizon surface), firewalls at the horizon, and remnants that retain information after evaporation. No single solution is universally accepted yet.
